newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SURGING SAFRICA CAR SALES GIVE NO HINT OF SLOWDOWN.
newsitem.headline: SURGING SAFRICA CAR SALES GIVE NO HINT OF SLOWDOWN.

text.p: Surging South African car sales give no indication of an expected slowdown in consumer spending in the face of a continuing restrictive monetary policy.

New passenger car sales reached a 14-year high of 27,816 in October, up 28.4 percent year-on-year and almost 40 percent month-on-month, according to the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa (NAAMSA).
Industry officials put the leap in sales down to intense competition in the motor industry.
"What we are curently experiencing is the result of the relentless competition which has been unleashed on the market," said Graham Hardy, marketing director of Volkswagen of South Africa (Pty) Ltd.
"Two years ago there were some seven manufacturers offering 180 models while today there are 19 manufacturers and importers offering 290 models."
Volkswagen was market leader last month, just ahead of Toyota South Africa .

Hardy said sales were boosted last month by the introduction of new models, intense price competiton on entry-level models and continued pre-emptive buying by consumers in anticipation of price increases as a result of the fall in the rand.
NAAMSA said it expected some consolidation in the market in forthcoming months following October's above-average sales.

Exchange rate related cost pressures could result in price increases in the months ahead, but for 1996 as a whole vehicle price inflation was expected to remain below the consumer price index, it said. Consumer price inflation stood at an annual 8.4 percent in September.
Total new passenger car sales rose to 208,483 units in the first 10 months of the year from 199,285 a year earlier.
